# 49｜Lesson 49：The Ideal Servant

> 📌 **《新概念英语三 · 双语精讲》系列 · 第 49 篇 / 共 60 篇**
> 📖 Lesson 49 · 38 句 · 15 词 · 3 个语法点 · 6 道自测题

## 01 课文精读 · Text

**1. It is a good thing my aunt Harriet died years ago.**

幸好我姑妈哈里特在多年前就去世了。

**2. If she were alive today she would not be able to air her views on her favourite topic of conversation: domestic servants.**

如果她今天还活着，她就不能再对她最喜欢的话题——佣人——发表意见了。

**3. Aunt Harriet lived in that leisurely age when servants were employed to do housework.**

哈里特姑妈生活在那个悠闲的时代，那时人们雇佣仆人来做家务。

**4. She had a huge, rambling country house called 'The Gables'.**

她有一幢名叫“山墙”的巨大而凌乱的乡村别墅。

**5. She was sentimentally attached to this house,**

她对这所房子感情深厚，

**6. for even though it was far too big for her needs, she persisted in living there long after her husband's death.**

因为尽管它对她来说太大了，但在她丈夫去世后很久，她仍然坚持住在那里。

**7. Before she grew old, aunt Harriet used to entertain lavishly.**

在她变老之前，哈里特姑妈经常大摆宴席。

**8. I often visited The Gables when I was a boy.**

我小时候经常去“山墙”探望。

**9. No matter how many guests were present, the great house was always immaculate.**

无论有多少客人，这幢大房子总是 immaculate（一尘不染的）。

**10. The parquet floors shone like mirrors;**

镶木地板擦得像镜子一样亮；

**11. highly polished silver was displayed in gleaming glass cabinets;**

擦得锃亮的银器摆放在闪闪发光的玻璃橱柜里；

**12. even my uncle's huge collection of books was kept miraculously free from dust.**

甚至我叔叔那一大批藏书也奇迹般地没有沾上一点灰尘。

**13. Aunt Harriet presided over an invisible army of servants that continuously scrubbed, cleaned, and polished.**

哈里特姑妈统管着一支无形的仆人队伍，他们不停地擦洗、清洁、打磨。

**14. She always referred to them as 'the shifting population',**

她总是称他们为“流动人口”，

**15. for they came and went with such frequency that I never even got a chance to learn their names.**

因为他们来去匆匆，我甚至都没机会记住他们的名字。

**16. Though my aunt pursued what was, in those days an enlightened policy,**

尽管我姑妈在那时实行着一项开明的政策，

**17. in that she never allowed her domestic staff to work more than eight hours a day, she was extremely difficult to please.**

即她从不允许她的家政人员每天工作超过八小时，但她还是非常难以取悦。

**18. While she always criticized the fickleness of human nature,**

虽然她总是批评人性的反复无常，

**19. she carried on an unrelenting search for the ideal servant to the end of her days,**

但她毕生都在不懈地寻找理想的仆人，

**20. even after she had been sadly disillusioned by Bessie.**

即使在她被贝茜伤透了心之后也是如此。

**21. Bessie worked for aunt Harriet for three years.**

贝茜为哈里特姑妈工作了三年。

**22. During that time she so gained my aunt's confidence, that she was put in charge of the domestic staff.**

在此期间，她深得姑妈的信任，被任命为家政人员的负责人。

**23. Aunt Harriet could not find words to praise Bessie's industriousness and efficiency.**

哈里特姑妈对贝茜的勤劳和效率赞不绝口。

**24. In addition to all her other qualifications, Bessie was an expert cook.**

除了她所有的其他优点，贝茜还是一位烹饪专家。

**25. She acted the role of the perfect servant for three years before Aunt Harriet discovered her 'little weakness'.**

她扮演了三年完美仆人的角色，直到哈里特姑妈发现了她的“小缺点”。

**26. After being absent from The Gables for a week,**

在离开“山墙”一周后，

**27. my aunt unexpectedly returned one afternoon with a party of guests and instructed Bessie to prepare dinner.**

姑妈在一个下午 unexpectedly（出乎意料地）带着一群客人回来了，并吩咐贝茜准备晚餐。

**28. Not only was the meal well below the usual standard, but Bessie seemed unable to walk steadily.**

晚餐不仅远低于平时的水准，而且贝茜似乎无法稳稳地走路。

**29. She bumped into the furniture and kept mumbling about the guests.**

她撞到了家具，嘴里不停地咕哝着关于客人的话。

**30. When she came in with the last course--a huge pudding--she tripped on the carpet**

当她端着最后一道菜——一个巨大的布丁——进来时，她在地毯上绊了一跤，

**31. and the pudding went flying through the air, narrowly missed my aunt, and crashed on the dining table with considerable force.**

布丁飞了起来，险些砸到我姑妈，然后重重地摔在了餐桌上。

**32. Though this caused great mirth among the guests, Aunt Harriet was horrified.**

尽管这让客人们大笑，但哈里特姑妈却吓坏了。

**33. She reluctantly came to the conclusion that Bessie was drunk.**

她 reluctantly（不情愿地）得出结论：贝茜喝醉了。

**34. The guests had, of course, realized this from the moment Bessie opened the door for them and, long before the final catastrophe,**

客人们当然从贝茜为他们开门的那一刻起就意识到了这一点，而且早在最后一场灾难发生之前，

**35. had had a difficult time trying to conceal their amusement.**

他们就一直在努力掩饰自己的 amused（好笑）。

**36. The poor girl was dismissed instantly.**

这个可怜的女孩被立刻解雇了。

**37. After her departure, Aunt Harriet discovered that there were piles of empty wine bottles of all shapes and sizes neatly stacked in what had once been Bessie's wardrobe.**

在她离开后，哈里特姑妈发现，曾是贝茜衣柜的地方，整齐地堆放着各种形状和大小的空酒瓶。

**38. They had mysteriously found their way there from the wine cellar!**

它们神秘地从酒窖里“溜”到了那里！

## 03 语法精讲 · Grammar

**1. 虚拟语气 (Subjunctive Mood) - 与现在事实相反**

`If + 主语 + 过去式(be用were), 主语 + would + 动词原形`

用于表达与事实相反的假设情况，主句用would+动词原形，从句用一般过去式

用来表达与现实相反的假设，常用于表达遗憾或不可能实现的愿望

**例句：If she were alive today she would not be able to air her views.**

如果她今天还活着，她就不能就她最喜欢的话题发表意见了。

**2. Not only...but (also) 引起的倒装句**

`Not only + 助动词/be动词/情态动词 + 主语 + 谓语...but (also) + 句子`

当not only放在句首时，它后面的句子要使用部分倒装语序

强调两个事实或情况，通常用于正式写作和演讲中增强语气

**例句：Not only was the meal well below the usual standard, but Bessie seemed unable to walk steadily.**

不仅饭菜远不如平时，而且贝齐看起来连路都走不稳。

**3. While 引导的让步状语从句**

`While + 主语 + 谓语..., 主句`

while 在此意为"虽然；尽管"，引导让步状语从句

用于引出让步或对比关系，while从句通常放在句首

**例句：While she always criticized the fickleness of human nature, she carried on an unrelenting search.**

虽然她总是批评人性的善变，但她仍在不懈地寻找。

## 04 句型模仿 · Patterns

- **It is a good thing + 主语 + 过去式**
  - 课文原句：It is a good thing my aunt Harriet died years ago.（好在哈丽雅特姑妈很多年前就去世了。）
  - 仿写：It is a good thing you came early.（好在你们来得早。）
- **No matter how + 形容词/副词 + 主语 + 谓语**
  - 课文原句：No matter how many guests were present, the great house was always immaculate.（无论有多少客人来访，这座大宅总是干干净净的。）
  - 仿写：No matter how hard he tried, he couldn't open the door.（无论他怎么努力，都打不开那扇门。）
- **After + 名词/动名词, 主语 + 谓语**
  - 课文原句：After her departure, Aunt Harriet discovered that there were piles of empty wine bottles.（在她离开后，姑妈哈丽雅特发现有一堆空酒瓶。）
  - 仿写：After finishing his homework, he went to play football.（完成作业后，他去踢足球了。）
- **主语 + be + so + 形容词/副词 + that + 句子**
  - 课文原句：The room was so dark that I couldn't see anything.（房间太暗了，我什么也看不见。）
  - 仿写：She spoke so quickly that I couldn't follow her.（她说得太快了，我跟不上。）
